tasks.title: Create src/todos.js and test/todos.test.js: the JSON store plus its tests
tasks.description: Create the persistence module src/todos.js plus its tests test/todos.test.js. The module reads and writes a JSON array of {id, text, done} objects. Because all work is confined to the project directory, the default store path is `.todos.json` in the current working directory, overridable with the TODO_FILE env var or an explicit argument. The module is pure logic with no console output and no process.exit; bin/todo.js owns argv parsing and printing. Tests point the store at test/.tmp/store inside the project so nothing is written outside it.

tasks.title: Create bin/todo.js, the command-line entry point
tasks.description: Create bin/todo.js: the executable entry point that parses process.argv, delegates to src/todos.js and prints one line per command. Handles add/list/done/remove/help, the --pending flag on list, and prints any thrown error to stderr with exit code 1. It never passes a filePath to the store functions, so it uses the default `.todos.json` in the current working directory.

edits.change:
Replace those three lines with the following, leaving the indented `npm test` line at the end of the file untouched (code examples are indented by four spaces, matching the existing Tests section):

A small Node project.

## todo

A small command-line todo list. Todos are stored as JSON in `.todos.json`, in the
directory you run the command from; set `TODO_FILE` to keep them elsewhere.

    node bin/todo.js add buy milk      # add a todo, prints its id
    node bin/todo.js list             # list every todo
    node bin/todo.js list --pending   # list only the todos that are not done
    node bin/todo.js done <id>        # mark the todo with <id> as done
    node bin/todo.js remove <id>      # delete the todo with <id>
    node bin/todo.js help             # print the usage

The same commands are available as `npm run todo -- <command>`, or as `todo
<command>` once the package is installed.

`add` prints the id of the new todo, and that id is what `done` and `remove`
take. `list` marks finished todos with a check mark and leaves the others with a
blank one, so the texts stay in a column:

    [8f2c1e6a-...] ✔ buy milk
    [1b9d7f30-...]   call the dentist

## Tests

contracts.statement: src/todos.js owns all persistence. It exports resolveStorePath(explicitPath), loadTodos(filePath), saveTodos(todos, filePath), addTodo(text, filePath), listTodos({ filePath, pending }), markDone(id, filePath), removeTodo(id, filePath) and formatTodo(todo). resolveStorePath returns, in order of preference: explicitPath if it is truthy, else process.env.TODO_FILE if set, else join(process.cwd(), '.todos.json'). Every other exported function resolves its path through resolveStorePath, so omitting filePath reads and writes the .todos.json file in the current working directory, and every function re-reads the file on each call so there is no shared in-memory cache. A todo is the object { id, text, done } where id is a randomUUID() string, text is the trimmed input and done is a boolean. DONE_MARK is the Unicode character U+2714 followed by one space, PENDING_MARK is a single space, and formatTodo returns the string [<id>] <mark> <text> with exactly one space before and after the mark. addTodo throws Error('todo text must not be empty') for whitespace-only text; markDone and removeTodo throw Error(`no todo with id ${id}`) when the id is not in the store.

bin/todo.js prints exactly one line per command so tests can assert on stdout: `add <text>` prints `added <id> <text>`; `done <id>` prints `done <id> <text>`; `remove <id>` prints `removed <id> <text>`; `list` prints one formatTodo line per todo and the single line `no todos` when there are none; `list --pending` filters to todos whose done is false; `help`, `--help` and `-h` print the usage text beginning with `Usage: todo <command> [options]`. Any thrown error is caught and printed to stderr as `todo: <message>` with process exit code 1; success sets exit code 0. bin/todo.js never passes a filePath to the store functions, so it uses the default location resolved by resolveStorePath.
